conventions.convention: Strong typicality excludes zero-probability atoms exactly and bounds each positive empirical frequency by a relative tolerance δP(a); blocklengths satisfy n ≥ 1.

Wyner-Ziv rates use natural logarithms and nats. The deterministic encoder observes X^n only; the decoder observes the message and Y^n. Distortion is expected normalized additive distortion, with finite nonempty alphabets and bounded d(x, x̂) independent of Y.
Operational achievability permits increasing blocklength subsequences, rate limsups bounded by the target rates, and expected-distortion limsups bounded by the target distortions.

Covering selects the least successful codeword index; conditional on success, the selected word has the marginal product law conditioned on the conditional typical set and is uniform within each conditional type class.

Packing uses codebooks independent of the source and independent uniform bin labels. Selected indices do not depend on bins; for each nonempty proper changed subset J, complementary selected words depend only on source-selection data and complementary codebooks.

Berger-Tung uses product test channels P_X∏i P_{U_i|X_i}; the complement of the full terminal set is a singleton. Its subset region and convex hull are achievable inner bounds, without a general exactness claim.

load_bearing.statement: Under the stated source/codebook independence, bin independence, and complementary-selection hypotheses, if every nonempty J satisfies Σi∈J n⁻¹ ln(M_i/B_i) < Σi∈J H(U_i) − H(U_J|U_{Jᶜ},S) − η for a common η > 0, then for every sufficiently small fixed positive typicality tolerance the expected number of wrong jointly typical tuples in the received bins, multiplied by the indicator that the selected true tuple and S^n are jointly typical, tends to zero.

For every finite P_XU, η > 0, and target tolerance ε > 0, sufficiently typical source blocks admit a match in an independent marginal codebook of rate R > I(X;U)+η with probability tending to one uniformly over those blocks. Conditional on a match, the least successful word has law P_U^⊗n conditioned on the conditional typical set and is uniform within each conditional type class.

For a finite Markov law P_XYZ=P_XY P_{Z|X} and every ε > 0, there are δ > 0 and n₀ such that a δ-typical fixed pair (x^n,y^n), together with a random Z^n supported on the δ-conditional typical set and uniform within each conditional type class, is ε-jointly typical with probability at least 1−C/n, uniformly over the admissible blocks and types.

Every finite feasible Wyner-Ziv test channel can be replaced by one with |U′| ≤ |X|+1, exactly the same expected distortion, and I(X;U′|Y) ≤ I(X;U|Y). Consequently the feasible infimum is attained with this cardinality bound.
D_min ≤ D_max; R_WZ is nonincreasing and convex on [D_min,∞), is zero for D ≥ D_max, and is continuous at every feasible distortion, including D_min and D_max.
For an attainable empirical distribution q on a finite nonempty alphabet of size m and n ≥ 1, (n+1)⁻ᵐ exp(nH(q)) ≤ |T_q| ≤ exp(nH(q)), with natural logarithms and 0 ln 0 := 0.

For a finite IID pair, finite reproduction alphabet, bounded distortion independent of Y, and decoder-only side information, R_WZ^op(D)=R_WZ(D)=min I(X;U|Y) over U−X−Y, |U| ≤ |X|+1, and deterministic reconstructions g(Y,U) of distortion at most D, for every D ≥ D_min. No code attains D < D_min.

For the stated finite IID multiterminal model, product test channels, and reconstruction maps of distortions at most D_i, every nonnegative rate vector satisfying Σi∈S R_i ≥ I(X_S;U_S|U_{Sᶜ}) for every nonempty S is achievable. The convex hull of the union of these regions is achievable.

seams_checked.note: The normalized additive distortion definition is preserved. The prerequisite page explicitly uses bits for finite rate-distortion quantities; this batch explicitly uses nats, and its no-side-information example defines the ordinary information rate in nats rather than silently importing a bit-valued formula.

IID source, separate-encoder, support, and Slepian-Wolf subset interfaces agree. The Wyner-Ziv proof explicitly converts the supplier's absolute empirical tolerance into relative typicality using the smallest positive joint mass. Endpoint examples use the lossless theorem separately from expected-Hamming-distortion achievability.

This is a reading-context prerequisite: the assigned items do not invoke its channel-capacity results. The pages agree on natural-log rates; no Gaussian, feedback, cost, or AC-dependent conclusion is imported into the finite choice-free source-coding arguments.

The actual item edges are from lem-it-cover-elgamal-salehi-conditional-packing to the strong-typicality definition and type-class bounds. Its F1–F2 faithfully retain relative tolerance, exact support restriction, and the type-count/cardinality upper bounds. It supplies a separate conditional-kernel packing argument rather than applying the independent marginal-bin lemma to source-indexed codebooks.
